clue.text: Formal document containing a Catholic's letter

indicators.note: the document is said to hold the other pieces, so they sit inside its letters

parts.note: a charter is a formal written grant of rights

explanation.surface: A papal or legal deed that includes a letter written by a Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like part of the document picture, but it is the definition: a single letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol, such as any letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Currencies firm for a long time

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
'in ages', as in 'I haven't seen you in ages'

explanation.surface: Monies of a business that has lasted many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Coinages are systems of money issued by a state, so they are currencies.

clue.text: When to get son donkey

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left, it rained'
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A question of when a boy will be given a pet donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is the everyday older name for the domestic donkey.

clue.text: Lawless American agent held in custody at first

parts.note: a narc is US slang for a narcotics agent

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the words held, in and custody is taken

explanation.surface: A US agent, outside the law, has been locked up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes a state with no order or rule of law, so lawless.

clue.text: Inclination to drill until Thursday

indicators.note: drilling bores into something, so the letters are found by going into the words until Thursday

explanation.surface: Someone is in the mood to practise drilling until the end of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' reads as practice or a power tool, but it signals going into the following words to find the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is a slope or lean, so an inclination.

clue.text: Sensitive Conservative regularly dithers about thick-skinned individual

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a sore spot is a sensitive one

indicators.note: every other letter of dithers is kept, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A touchy Tory politician wavers over some insensitive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SORE + CON + IHR, the even letters of 'dithers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is famous for its tough hide; thick-skinned here is literal, with a nod to the figurative sense.

clue.text: An Arabic drink knocked over in Asian city

indicators.note: a glass knocked over ends up the other way round, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: arak is an aniseed spirit of the Middle East

explanation.surface: A spilled glass of Middle Eastern spirit in a city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses ARAK to give KARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara, the Turkish capital, stands in Anatolia, the Asian part of Turkey.

clue.text: Pothead captured in bust on Erraid

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words bust on Erraid

explanation.surface: A cannabis user caught in a police raid on a small Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Erraid is a tiny island off Mull, in western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoner is slang for a habitual cannabis smoker, the same as pothead.

clue.text: Donation perhaps left in error

parts.note: the left is one hand, as in 'on the left hand'
a sum that is out is wrong

explanation.surface: A gift, possibly left behind by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a handout is one kind of donation.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is money or goods given free to those in need, one kind of gift.

clue.text: Black underpants supporting several balls — that's too much of a load

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters it follows are scrambled

parts.note: taken from the first half of underpants

explanation.surface: Dark underwear sits beneath a load of balls, an excessive burden.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'underpants': 'under' is the fodder and 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) signals the shuffle, giving URDEN. 'supporting' places B and URDEN beneath the cricket over in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An overburden is an excessive weight or demand, more than can be borne.

clue.text: Plant stylish hedge

parts.note: in means fashionable
to hedge is to stall or avoid committing oneself

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to put in a smart row of shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'hedge' paint a garden, but 'Plant' means to set in place and 'hedge' means to prevaricate.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something, like a device or a spy, is to put it in place or fix it.

clue.text: Crumpled banknote wrapped around a toxic food additive

indicators.note: the shuffled letters enclose the following piece
a crumpled note has its shape mixed up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screwed-up banknote has been used to wrap a poisonous ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: This seed gives a vanilla-like flavouring, but its coumarin is toxic and it is banned as an additive in the US.

clue.text: One fleeced Al Capone, one conceded, when returning alcohol, primarily

indicators.note: what is left comes back the other way, read right to left
conceded means given up, so the word one is surrendered from Capone
only the first letter of alcohol is used

explanation.surface: Gangster Al Capone cheated someone, who gave in when the bootleg liquor came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one conceded' removes ONE from CAPONE, leaving CAP; 'returning' turns it into PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpaca is a South American animal kept for its wool, so one that gets shorn.

clue.text: Toy weapon has unusual rings to crack safe

indicators.note: cracking a safe opens it, letting the other letters in

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: the letters of has are made unusual by mixing them

parts.note: O looks like a ring, so two rings give OO

explanation.surface: A toy gun with odd rings is used in a safe-cracking job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges 'has'; 'peter' for a safe is old British underworld slang, which the safe-cracking picture hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a small tube for blowing dried peas, a classic child's plaything.

clue.text: Fail to secure weapon? Not I — it can go off without reason

definitions.text: it can go off without reason

indicators.note: not here tells you to leave out the letter named next

parts.note: to seal is to secure, as with a closed envelope
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Someone fails to lock up a gun, protesting it wasn't them, and it goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I' removes the I from FAIL to give FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is an alert raised when there is no real danger, like a bell ringing for nothing.

clue.text: Cleaner receives award from the queen in assembly room

indicators.note: the cleaner takes the award into her letters

parts.note: a char is British for a cleaning lady
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour conferred by the monarch

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman is honoured by the monarch in a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a large room for formal meetings, such as a council's debating hall.

clue.text: Wipe out many years, say, when time drifts away

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

indicators.note: the letter drifts out of the word, leaving it shorter

parts.note: to dictate is to say aloud for writing down
T is the physics symbol for time

explanation.surface: Many years get erased when time just slips by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a verb here, not the usual 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something is to destroy it completely, to obliterate it.

clue.text: Heroes in fancy restaurant

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Heroes are dining out at a smart restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: This spelling of the word is listed in Collins.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosherie is a slang word for an eating place, from nosh, food.

clue.text: A falling pound stops professional recess

indicators.note: the pound goes in to stop the gap between the other two pieces

parts.note: pro is short for professional
an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church
L is the symbol for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A sliding currency puts a halt to a professional's holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolapse is the slipping down of an organ from its normal position, so a falling.

clue.text: Do reports badly, leading to instruction to sell shares

indicators.note: doing something badly makes a mess of it, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Botched reports lead a trader to tell the broker to dump stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop order tells a broker to sell once a price falls to a set level, limiting losses.

clue.text: Thailand's currency in difficulty

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: The Thai baht is in a spot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thailand's currency' reads as the baht; it is two pieces, Thailand giving T and currency giving the Russian unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a problem or difficulty, as in 'in trouble'.

clue.text: Asian drunk discussed office worker

indicators.note: talked about, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a Thai is someone from Thailand; pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: People talked about an Asian in the office who was intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai pissed' spoken quickly gives the sound of the answer; 'pissed' meaning drunk is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist keys in documents, a classic clerical job in an office.

clue.text: Streams silent movie star

definitions.meaning: Louise ..., the bob-haired American actress of 1920s silent films

explanation.surface: A silent film actress pours out tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooks are small streams, and Louise Brooks was a famous silent-era screen actress.

clue.text: TV station expels new fashion designer

indicators.note: one letter is thrown out of the station's name

parts.note: a television station broadcasts on a channel

explanation.surface: A broadcaster sacks a newcomer who designs clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco Chanel was the French couturier behind the little black dress and the fashion house of that name.

clue.text: Bore pilot silly, which is novel

indicators.note: boring someone silly scrambles them, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dull story bores an airman out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the adjective meaning new but is the noun, a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a quickly written book produced just to make money.

clue.text: Care for back

definitions.meaning: bring up a child or animal, look after

explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise and care for them; the rear is the back of something.

clue.text: Teletubby twice to regret making comeback to make catchy music

indicators.note: coming back means the letters run in the other direction
the name is given two times over

parts.note: Po is the smallest of the Teletubbies, from the BBC children's show
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A children's TV character regrets two comebacks with a pop tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Teletubbies is a British pre-school TV series. 'making comeback' reverses POPORUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Europop is light, catchy pop music from continental Europe, ABBA-style.

clue.text: Head of Parlophone loves scat

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: The boss of a record label is fond of scat singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Parlophone is a British record label; 'scat' suggests jazz singing but means droppings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is animal droppings, the same as the childish word for excrement.

clue.text: Small three-wheeler beginning to roll forward

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a trike is a tricycle

indicators.note: only the start of the word roll is used

explanation.surface: A little tricycle starts to move ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' reads as a direction but is the football position.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a striker is an attacking forward whose job is to score goals.

clue.text: Spooner's crude technique that's used to send messages

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the initial sounds of words

parts.note: coarse means crude or vulgar
a mode is a method or way of doing something

explanation.surface: A rough method someone uses for sending messages.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COARSE MODE gives MORSE CODE.
explanation.definitionFit: The system of dots and dashes was used to send telegraph and radio messages.
